title: Witnessed adjunctions and the exceptional comparison on one affine chart
statement:
Fix the finite purity coefficients [def-pur-conventions]: $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and $n\geq1$; put $A=A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$. For every finite-type $k$-scheme $S$, let $\nu_S:S_{\mathrm{proet}}\to S_{\mathrm{et}}$ be the comparison morphism [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism] and let $\mathcal C(S)=\mathcal D^+_{\mathrm{et}}(S,A)$ be the witnessed category [def-sf-etale-origin-subcategory]: an object consists of $K\in D^+(S_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$, $K_e\in D^+(S_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ and an isomorphism $\nu_S^*K_e\cong K$, and morphisms are the morphisms of the underlying pro-etale complexes. For a separated finite-type $k$-morphism $v:S\to R$ [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties], use compact support $Rv_!$ [def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed]. At a chosen compactification write $v_e^\times$ for the ordinary etale right adjoint and write $G_v=\nu_S^*v_e^\times R\nu_{R,*}$ for the transported exceptional functor [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image], initially on bounded-below objects. Then $Rv_!$ and $G_v$ admit lifts to $\mathcal C(S)\to\mathcal C(R)$ and $\mathcal C(R)\to\mathcal C(S)$, respectively, with natural adjunction bijections
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C(R)}(Rv_!M,N)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C(S)}(M,G_vN).$$
Their underlying functors and bijections are independent of compactification under the canonical comparison isomorphisms. If $M\cong\nu_S^*M_e$ and $N\cong\nu_R^*N_e$ are the specified witnesses, their images have witnesses $Rv_{!,e}M_e$ and $v_e^\times N_e$, both bounded below.

Let $f:X\to Y$ be separated of finite type between finite-type $k$-schemes. Choose an affine open immersion $g:V\hookrightarrow Y$, put $X_V=X\times_YV$, and write $h:X_V\hookrightarrow X$ and $f_V:X_V\to V$ for the projections. Choose an affine open immersion $u':U\hookrightarrow X_V$, an integer $d\geq0$, and a closed immersion $i:U\hookrightarrow T=\mathbf A^d_V$ [def-sbc-affine-space] with projection $\pi:T\to V$ such that $f_Vu'=\pi i$; put $u=hu'$. Open inverse image [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image] preserves $\mathcal C$ and the witness restricts to the ordinary etale restriction. There is a natural isomorphism on $\mathcal C(V)$
$$L(u')^*G_{f_V}N\cong G_iG_\pi N.$$
For every bounded constructible $L\in D^b_c(Y,A)$ [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility], the canonical base-open and chart comparisons give
$$Lh^*G_fL\cong G_{f_V}Lg^*L,\qquad Lu^*G_fL\cong G_iG_\pi Lg^*L.$$
All these comparisons are comparisons in the witnessed categories; no preservation of bounded constructibility by $G_f$, $G_i$ or $G_\pi$ is assumed in these assertions.

proof.text: Every scheme here and every open subscheme is Noetherian, hence quasi-compact and quasi-separated: [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] over $\operatorname{Spec}k$ (a field is Noetherian) and [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-open-subscheme-noetherian]; so open immersions are quasi-compact, hence of finite type. [lem-pod-separated-finite-type-base-change] makes $f_V$ separated of finite type and [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-base-change] makes $h$ open; the closed immersion $i$, the projection $\pi$ and the composite $f_Vu'=\pi i$ are separated of finite type. [thm-nagata-compactification] supplies compactifications $c=(j,p)$ of $v$ and of $f,f_V,i,\pi$; $\overline S$ is of finite type over $k$, so $\dim\overline S\leq d$ for some $d$ by [lem-kun-dimension-finite-type]. Neither $X$ nor $Y$ need be separated over $k$.

proof.text: Use [lem-pur-witnessed-open-chart-transport] for open restriction, retaining the ordinary etale restricted witness and its identity and composition compatibilities. Its chart assertion, with $X$ replaced by $X_V$, $j=u'$ and $f=f_V$, gives $L(u')^*G_{f_V}N\cong G_iG_\pi N$ naturally for every $N\in\mathcal C(V)$. Its bounded-below Hom normalization and comparison-unit identifications ensure this is an isomorphism in $\mathcal C(U)$ without assuming constructible preservation.

source.place: Step 1 (witnessed adjunction and chart) and Step 3 (base-open passage)

proof.text: For the final assertion, [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin] puts the bounded constructible $L$ in $\mathcal C(Y)$. Step 3 puts $Lg^*L$ in $\mathcal C(V)$. Apply only the independent bounded-class clause of [cor-exc-base-change-open-immersion-general], with $g:V\hookrightarrow Y$ and $h:X_V\hookrightarrow X$. It states that the canonical map $Lh^*G_fL\to G_{f_V}Lg^*L$ is invertible for this bounded constructible input. Steps 2 and 3 show that its source and target carry etale-origin witnesses; their Hom sets are the underlying pro-etale Hom sets, so its inverse is also a morphism of the witnessed categories. Restrict it along $u'$ and compose with step 3 at $N=Lg^*L$. Using $u=hu'$ and the composition compatibility of step 3 gives $Lu^*G_fL\cong G_iG_\pi Lg^*L$, as required.
